thread:
Taylor: Quick sync after RFC merge: need concrete auto-fallback behaviour for A/B canaries. Requirements: tiny blast radius, cheap runtime checks, clear audit trail.
Mira: Control-plane should hold policy, runtime only runs fast detectors + catastrophic short-circuit.
Sam: Concern: control-plane latency on sudden spikes. Runtime must act sub-30s for severe QoS regressions.
Jordan: Hybrid: runtime detects and emits a candidate event; control-plane confirms or issues undo. Runtime can short-circuit only for severe patterns.
Priya: Telemetry: per-route QPS, p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, sampled quality flags. Use 60s windows with a 5m rolling baseline.
Taylor: Proposed auto-exit rules: (A) error_rate > 2% over 2m AND >2x baseline; OR (B) p95 latency +300ms AND >1.5x baseline. Manual override allowed.
Sam: Add anti-flap: require 3 consecutive violating windows before auto-rollback.
Mira: Add degrade path: for modest regressions drop canary traffic by a step (e.g., -20%) instead of full rollback.
Jordan: API sketch: control-plane /v1/fallbacks; runtime subscribes SSE. Example: {"variant":"canary-2026-01","action":"reduce","pct":20,"expires_at":1760000000}
Jordan: Short-circuit must be idempotent with deterministic reason codes like short_circuit:error_spike.
Priya: Quality regressions: sampled human eval + heuristics; require human confirmation for ambiguous quality issues before full rollback.
sre-bot: Updated playbook: auto-rollback posts to #oncall + captures traces and links runbook https://runbooks/relaunch :rotating_light:
Taylor: Next steps: Sam to write RFC with exact metrics/windows/thresholds + API schema. Runtime team to implement short-circuit tests. SRE to map alerts to playbook. 30m sync tomorrow.
Sam: On it, will share first draft EOD.
Mira: Let's ensure audit logs include reason, deltas, and who/what authorized action.
Taylor: Agreed. Thanks team.
